Assessment revised with Beige Book insights:
- The FOMC’s June 15, 2022 statement highlights stronger activity and robust job gains with a very tight labor market, alongside elevated inflation driven by supply-demand imbalances, higher energy prices, and global shocks (Ukraine war; China lockdowns). Policy tightening accelerated with a 75 bp hike to 1.50–1.75% and balance sheet runoff.
- Beige Book references indicate firms continue to hire and are offering flexibility to attract/retain workers, with widespread wage increases and noted wage growth. This corroborates tight labor conditions and persistent cost pressures.
- District reports also point to businesses passing through higher input and fuel costs (e.g., fuel surcharges), reinforcing broad-based price pressures. COVID-related disruptions, including China lockdowns, are seen as exacerbating supply chains and weighing on consumers in some areas.
- SLOOS suggests domestic bank credit supply remained accommodative in Q1 (eased standards for C&I and multifamily CRE; stronger loan demand; lower line-of-credit costs), cushioning near-term activity despite tighter financial conditions from markets and policy.
Net read: While growth is supported by ongoing hiring and accommodative bank credit, the Beige Book’s strong wage and price pass-through dynamics amplify the inflation problem and validate a more hawkish policy path. Overall tone remains negative and slightly more so than a SLOOS-only overlay given persistent inflation pressures.
